title: Daily automatic backup, with last-backup time and a one-tap backup on the dashboard
description: Product Owner request: should backup run automatically, daily; show the last backup time on the home screen with a small icon to back up from there. RECOMMENDED: yes, and it is the single highest-value safety feature left. Today backup is entirely manual - BackupScreen fires ActivityResultContracts.CreateDocument, the warden picks a location, and nothing records that it happened. A warden who forgets for two months has two months of unrecoverable data on one phone, and nothing in the app tells them so. WHY IT NEEDS A DESIGN, not just a WorkManager job: the current export takes a one-shot Uri from CreateDocument and no persistable permission is taken, so there is no folder to write to unattended. The job needs a location chosen ONCE via OpenDocumentTree with takePersistableUriPermission, stored in a new BackupPreferences, and reused daily. Everything else reuses BackupManager.export() as-is. THE REAL RISK is not the job failing, it is the job failing SILENTLY - a warden who believes they are covered and is not, is worse off than one who knows they are not. So the dashboard tile is not decoration, it is the feature: it must show staleness and failure as prominently as success, using the existing RAG tokens (recent = green, getting old = amber, never/failed/very stale = red). SUGGESTED SHAPE: (1) pick a folder once, persisted; (2) daily WorkManager job, same pattern as LODGY-15/59/60; (3) skip the run when nothing has changed since the last backup, so identical zips are not churned daily - the zip carries photos and is not small; (4) keep a rolling window of the last N backups and delete older ones, or storage grows without bound; (5) if the folder becomes unwritable - card removed, folder deleted, permission revoked - surface that on the dashboard rather than retrying quietly. RELATION TO LODGY-66: this is the auto-export measure recommended there. It also strengthens the case against soft delete, because a recent automatic backup covers the accidental-deletion fear that a recycle bin was meant to address, without taxing every query in the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Warden picks a backup folder once; the permission persists across reboots and app updates, and the choice is changeable later from More
A daily WorkManager job writes a timestamped backup zip into that folder without any interaction, following the existing periodic-worker pattern
The dashboard shows when the last backup succeeded, in plain relative language, with a backup icon that runs one immediately
The dashboard indicator distinguishes recent, getting stale, and never-or-failed using the LODGY-36 status tokens, so a silently broken backup is visible rather than assumed fine
A run is skipped when no data has changed since the last successful backup, so unchanged days do not accumulate identical zips
Only the most recent N backups are kept; older ones are removed so the folder does not grow without bound
If the folder becomes unwritable the failure is surfaced on the dashboard and the warden is told how to re-pick it - it never fails silently
Backward compatible: an existing install that has never chosen a folder keeps working exactly as today, prompted but never blocked, and no migration is required beyond the new preference

history.note: Requested by the PO: daily auto-backup, last-backup time on the home screen with a one-tap backup icon. Filed with a recommended design and the silent-failure risk called out, because an auto-backup a warden wrongly believes is running is worse than no auto-backup.

Cross-reference: LODGY-76 (forgotten PIN) is another argument for this ticket. A warden locked out of their own app loses everything only if there is no recent backup - with a daily automatic one, a forgotten PIN costs them the app state and nothing else.

Starting. Building the PO's recommended shape: folder picked once via OpenDocumentTree + takePersistableUriPermission stored in a new BackupPreferences; a daily WorkManager job (AutoBackupWorker) following the LODGY-15/59/60 pattern; a dashboard tile using the LODGY-36 RAG tokens that shows staleness/failure as prominently as success and a backup icon that runs one immediately; skip-when-unchanged via a content fingerprint; a rolling window of the last N zips; folder-unwritable surfaced on the dashboard, never silent. Orchestration goes in a testable AutoBackup class; only the SAF/DocumentFile glue (SafBackupStore) is the thin, excluded wrapper, matching the PhotoStorage/LodgyNotifications precedent. No migration - just the new preference (AC8).

Built the PO's recommended shape and verified it end to end on the emulator against the live populated database.

WHAT WAS BUILT.
- BackupPreferences (new DataStore 'backup_prefs'): folderUri, lastSuccessTime, lastFingerprint, lastAttemptFailed. No Room change, no migration (AC8).
- SafBackupStore (thin, excluded from coverage like PhotoStorage): takePersistableUriPermission, isWritable, createBackupFile, listBackupNames, deleteBackups via DocumentFile. Added androidx.documentfile 1.0.1.
- AutoBackup (orchestrator, fully unit-tested over mocked deps): NOT_CONFIGURED / SKIPPED_UNCHANGED / SUCCESS / FAILED. Skip via content fingerprint; prune to KEEP_BACKUPS=7; records success/failure.
- BackupManager.currentFingerprint(): checkpoints the WAL then SHA-256 over the db bytes + photo name/size list, so a WAL-only change still counts and identical data skips (AC5).
- AutoBackupWorker + WorkManager.scheduleAutoBackup(), scheduled unconditionally in LodgyApplication (AC2). Always returns success so a failure surfaces on the dashboard, not via a silent retry (AC7).
- Dashboard tile (DashboardViewModel/Screen): backupHealth() maps to the LODGY-36 RAG tokens - green recent, amber stale/not-set-up, red never/failed; a one-tap icon runs backupNow(force) when configured, else routes to the Backup screen (AC3/AC4).
- Folder chooser on the Backup screen (More -> Backup): OpenDocumentTree + persist grant, shows on/off and change-folder (AC1).

VERIFIED ON DEVICE (Hindi UI):
- Tile starts 'Not set up' (amber); its icon routes to the Backup screen; picked Download/LodgyBackups, the system 'Allow Lodgy to access folder?' grant was taken, and the screen switched to 'folder set, daily backups on'.
- Tile then read NEVER (red). Tapped 'back up now' -> a real lodgy-backup-2026-09-05-173522.zip appeared in the folder (pulled it: contains lodgy.db at the live 192512 bytes), and the tile turned green 'Last backup 0 minutes ago'.
- AC7: deleted the folder, tapped 'back up now' -> tile shows red 'Last backup failed - check the folder', no crash. Re-picked a folder afterwards and it backs up green again, so the emulator is left in a working state.

NOT drivable from a JVM/adb session, covered by unit tests instead: the daily periodic trigger (WorkSchedulerTest asserts the unique 1-day job), skip-unchanged and prune-to-7 (AutoBackupTest + AutoBackupHealthTest), fingerprint stability (BackupManagerTest).

481 tests pass (was 453; +28), line coverage 96.96% (gate 0.93), jacocoCoverageVerification green, assembleDebug OK.

Docs updated in step: DESIGN.md 4.8 + three decision-log rows; USER-MANUAL.md 8; and a 'Keeping your data safe' section in docs/design/screenshots.html showing the green and red tile states. No DATA-MODEL.md change - the feature adds a DataStore preference, not a Room column.

QA NOTE: the on-device screenshots are in Hindi because the emulator's stored language is Hindi and the in-app English toggle did not re-apply on recreate() this session - that is pre-existing behaviour unrelated to this ticket, but worth a glance if you can reproduce it.

FAIL on AC7. Verified everything else on the emulator and it holds: folder picked once with a persisted read/write SAF grant and changeable from More (AC1); daily unique WorkManager job (AC2); the dashboard tile shows the last-backup time with a one-tap icon (AC3); RAG states read correctly - green 'Last backup 0 minutes ago', red on a deleted folder, amber when not set up (AC4); skip-unchanged and keep-7 are unit-tested and the fingerprint is stable (AC5/AC6); an install with no folder is a no-op with no migration (AC8).

THE DEFECT (AC7 - 'the warden is TOLD HOW TO RE-PICK it'): the failure is surfaced, but the warden is given no way to fix it from where it is shown. In the FAILED state the tile reads 'Last backup failed - check the folder', and its icon (configured==true) calls backupNow(), which just fails again. There is no route to the folder chooser and no instruction to change it - a warden whose SD card was pulled or folder deleted taps the icon, watches it go red again, and dead-ends. Repro: set a folder, delete it (rm -rf the tree), tap the tile icon -> red, tap again -> red, with no path forward on the dashboard.

FIX DIRECTION: in the FAILED state, route the tile (or a clear affordance on it) to the folder picker, and/or make the message actionably say to re-pick, so re-picking is reachable from the dashboard where the problem appears. The picking UI itself already exists on the Backup screen.

AC7 gap fixed and verified on the emulator. QA was right: in the failed state the tile retried against the missing folder and never offered a way to re-pick it.

FIX: the tile's action is now state-aware. When the backup has never worked (NOT_CONFIGURED) or the last run FAILED, the icon sends the warden to the folder picker (Backup screen) instead of retrying; a set-up, working backup still runs on the spot. The failed message now reads 'Last backup failed - tap to choose the folder again' (Hindi too), and choosing a folder clears the failure flag (BackupPreferences.setFolderUri) so the tile recovers immediately rather than staying red until the next successful run.

VERIFIED END TO END: set a folder, deleted it, tapped 'back up now' -> tile went red with the new actionable text and the icon's action became 'Choose the backup folder again'. Tapped it -> landed on the Backup screen's Change-folder control (not a silent retry). Re-picked the folder -> tile cleared back to a normal state; tapped 'back up now' -> green 'Last backup 0 minutes ago' and a fresh zip written. So the full broken -> recover loop now works from the dashboard where the failure shows.

489 tests pass, line coverage 97.00% (gate 0.93), jacocoCoverageVerification green, assembleDebug OK. New BackupPreferences test covers the failed-flag-cleared-on-repick. Docs updated: DESIGN.md 4.8 now describes the re-pick action, and the failed-tile screenshot + caption in screenshots.html were refreshed to the new text.

PASS - re-verified the AC7 fix on the emulator and re-confirmed the rest still holds.

AC7 (the fail reason) is now met: broke the folder (deleted the tree), tapped 'back up now' -> the tile turned red with 'Last backup failed - tap to choose the folder again' and its action changed to 'Choose the backup folder again'. Tapping it routed to the Backup screen's change-folder control instead of a silent retry. Re-picked the folder -> the red state cleared immediately; a subsequent 'back up now' went green with a fresh zip on disk. The broken -> re-pick -> recover loop is reachable entirely from the dashboard where the failure shows.

Rest still good from the prior pass: persisted SAF grant and change-from-More (AC1); daily unique job (AC2); last-backup time + one-tap icon (AC3); RAG green/amber/red states (AC4); skip-unchanged and keep-7 unit-tested (AC5/AC6); no-op with no folder and no migration (AC8).

489 tests pass, line coverage 97.00%, jacocoCoverageVerification green.

BOUNCED, and it is a small fix on an otherwise good feature. The tile on Home reads 'Automatic backup / Not set up - tap to choose a folder'. I tapped the words. Nothing happened. I tapped the card. Nothing happened. The card and its text are not tappable at all - the only clickable thing is a small icon at the far right (labelled 'Set up automatic backup'), which does take me to the right screen. So the app tells me to tap something that is not a tap target. I sat there tapping the sentence like it was broken. The icon reads as a 'do it now' button from its position, not as the way to answer the instruction next to it. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: this is the one tile whose whole job is to stop me losing everything if my phone dies, and the app is nagging me daily about it. If the nag does not work when I respond to it, I will assume the feature is broken and stop noticing the tile - which leaves me with no backup, which is the exact thing this ticket exists to prevent. It is also the population LODGY-80 was written for: I am not going to hunt for a small icon when the words told me to tap. FIX: make the whole card tap to the same place the icon already goes. Everything else about this holds up - the tile is honest that nothing is set up, the wording tells me to pick a cloud-synced folder, and the manual backup and restore both work (I did a full export and restore during this session and got my data back intact).

Fixed. The whole card is the tap target now, not just the icon - it routes to the folder picker when nothing is set up or the last run failed, and runs a backup on the spot when a folder is working, which is what the icon already did. One line; the UAT report was exact about what broke and why it mattered. Verified by repeating the warden's own action: tapped the words 'Not set up - tap to choose a folder' and landed on the Backup screen where 'Choose backup folder' lives. Full suite passes, coverage above the gate.

PASS. Re-ran the reproduction from the UAT bounce: tapping the status text now goes where the text says. The icon still works and still means the same thing, and the routing rule is unchanged - not-configured and failed go to the picker, a healthy backup runs immediately - so nothing else about the tile moved.

Accepted. I tapped the sentence that told me to tap and it did what it said. That is the whole complaint closed. The rest of this feature I already trusted - the tile is honest when nothing is set up, and the manual backup and restore both got my data back intact during UAT.
